items.heading: Crop rotation
details: Improves nutrient management in the soil and disrupts pest and disease cycles between seasons.

items.heading: Mixed cropping
details: Growing several crops together increases agricultural diversity and reduces dependence on any single crop.

items.heading: Cereal-pulse intercropping
details: Different crops use soil resources differently, while legumes can contribute nitrogen back to the soil.

items.heading: Traditional seed preservation
details: Saving and exchanging seed each season preserves agricultural genetic diversity for the future.

items.heading: Neem-based pest control
details: Neem compounds can interfere with insect feeding, growth, and reproduction, offering a natural pesticide.

items.heading: Farmyard manure
details: Adds organic matter and nutrients back into the soil, improving its long-term structure and fertility.

items.heading: Composting
details: Converts organic waste into a useful, nutrient-rich soil amendment.

items.heading: Mulching
details: A covering layer over soil reduces evaporation, suppresses weeds, and protects the soil surface.

items.heading: Agroforestry
details: Combining trees and crops on the same land can provide shade, biodiversity, and soil benefits together.

items.heading: Traditional mixed farming with livestock
details: Crop residues can feed livestock, while their manure returns nutrients back to the fields.
